description: Machine-readable inventory of testing audit checks for validation and generated maps.

statusTaxonomy.present: The expected invariant is fully satisfied.
statusTaxonomy.partial: Most signals resolve, with a small number of exceptions, or the codebase shows mixed adherence to a soft check.

enrichmentFlags.description: Run the detected Vitest or Jest test runner in coverage mode and use the result to enrich coverage and test-count signals.

relatedAudits.relationship: Owns whether tests run at each development lifecycle stage.
Owns lint plugin configuration; overlapping plugin gaps are surfaced here too.
Owns whether tests catch error paths well.

checks.title: Single test runner installed
checks.expectation: Exactly one of Vitest or Jest is present in development dependencies.
checks.violationSignal: Both Vitest and Jest are present with no clear migration.

checks.title: React Testing Library installed
checks.expectation: When React is detected, @testing-library/react is present in development dependencies.
checks.violationSignal: A React project that ships tests is missing @testing-library/react.

checks.title: User Event installed
checks.expectation: @testing-library/user-event is available for interaction simulation.
checks.violationSignal: @testing-library/user-event is missing.

checks.title: Jest DOM installed
checks.expectation: @testing-library/jest-dom is available so assertions describe user-visible state with DOM-aware matchers.
checks.violationSignal: @testing-library/jest-dom is missing.

checks.title: Testing Library lint plugin configured
checks.expectation: eslint-plugin-testing-library is installed and enabled.
checks.violationSignal: eslint-plugin-testing-library is missing or not enabled.

checks.title: Jest DOM lint plugin configured
checks.expectation: eslint-plugin-jest-dom is installed and enabled.
checks.violationSignal: eslint-plugin-jest-dom is missing or not enabled.

checks.title: Jest DOM matchers loaded in setup file
checks.expectation: The test runner setup file imports @testing-library/jest-dom.
checks.violationSignal: No setup file exists, or the setup file does not import @testing-library/jest-dom.

checks.title: Coverage tool configured with thresholds
checks.expectation: The test runner has coverage configuration with explicit line, statement, branch, and function thresholds.
checks.violationSignal: Coverage is configured without thresholds, or no coverage configuration exists.

checks.title: End-to-end framework present
checks.expectation: Playwright or Cypress is present in development dependencies for user-facing applications.
checks.violationSignal: Neither Playwright nor Cypress is present in a user-facing application.

checks.title: Query distribution favours Priority 1
checks.expectation: At least the configured threshold percentage of all Testing Library queries are Priority 1 queries.
checks.violationSignal: Priority 1 query distribution is below the threshold.

checks.title: Test ID usage is rare
checks.expectation: At most the configured threshold percentage of all queries use getByTestId.
checks.violationSignal: getByTestId distribution is above the threshold.

checks.title: No querySelector for finding elements
checks.expectation: Tests use Testing Library queries instead of container.querySelector or document.querySelector for element lookup.
checks.violationSignal: querySelector calls are used in tests for element lookup.

checks.title: Queries via screen, not destructured
checks.expectation: Queries come from screen.getBy*, not destructured from the render return value.
checks.violationSignal: Patterns such as const { getByRole } = render(...) appear.

checks.title: Render return named view, not wrapper
checks.expectation: When the render return is captured, it is named view, or destructured for only what is needed.
checks.violationSignal: Patterns such as const wrapper = render(...) appear.

checks.title: ByRole is the dominant Priority 1 query
checks.expectation: Of Priority 1 queries, at least the configured threshold percentage are getByRole with the name option.
checks.violationSignal: Priority 1 queries are used without meaningful getByRole adoption.

checks.title: No redundant ARIA roles in test assertions
checks.expectation: Tests do not assert on role attributes that semantic elements already provide implicitly.
checks.violationSignal: Assertions match redundant roles such as [role="button"] on a button element.

checks.title: User Event preferred over Fire Event
checks.expectation: At least the configured threshold percentage of interaction calls use userEvent rather than fireEvent.
checks.violationSignal: The userEvent interaction ratio is below the threshold.

checks.title: find* used for elements not yet present
checks.expectation: When waiting for an element to appear, tests use findBy* instead of waitFor(() => getBy*()).
checks.violationSignal: waitFor callbacks contain only a getBy* lookup.

checks.title: query* only for absence assertions
checks.expectation: queryBy* is used only with not.toBeInTheDocument() or analogous absence checks.
checks.violationSignal: queryBy* is used in a positive-presence assertion.

checks.title: waitFor callback contains a single assertion
checks.expectation: Each waitFor callback wraps exactly one expect call.
checks.violationSignal: waitFor callbacks contain multiple expect calls.

checks.title: waitFor callback is not empty
checks.expectation: The assertion being retried is inside the waitFor callback.
checks.violationSignal: waitFor(() => {}) is followed by assertions outside the callback.

checks.title: No side effects in waitFor
checks.expectation: waitFor callbacks contain assertions only, not event simulation or state mutation.
checks.violationSignal: fireEvent or userEvent calls appear inside waitFor.

checks.title: No unnecessary act wrapping
checks.expectation: render and fireEvent calls are not wrapped in act(...), because React Testing Library already wraps them.
checks.violationSignal: Patterns such as act(() => { render(...) }) or act(() => { fireEvent.click(...) }) appear.

checks.title: No manual cleanup calls
checks.expectation: Tests do not import or call cleanup from @testing-library/react.
checks.violationSignal: cleanup is imported or called.

checks.title: Assertions are explicit
checks.expectation: Tests wrap relevant getBy* lookups with expect(...).toBeInTheDocument() or analogous assertions.
checks.violationSignal: getBy* calls appear on a line by themselves without expect.

checks.title: Tests describe user behaviour
checks.expectation: Test names describe user-visible behaviour rather than implementation details.
checks.violationSignal: Test names describe internal state changes or internal function calls.

checks.title: No assertions against hard-coded utility classes
checks.expectation: Class assertions use semantic theme tokens, or preferably role, label, or text assertions, instead of raw utility classes.
checks.violationSignal: toHaveClass assertions reference raw utility classes such as numeric colour scales, raw spacing utilities, or raw layout utilities.

checks.title: Snapshots are bounded and intentional
checks.expectation: Snapshot tests cover small, intentional, named outputs.
checks.violationSignal: A snapshot exceeds the configured line threshold, captures whole-component output, captures internal tree shape, or appears as the default assertion style.

checks.title: Coverage thresholds enforced in continuous integration
checks.expectation: The continuous-integration test step fails when coverage drops below the configured threshold.
checks.violationSignal: Coverage is configured, but continuous integration does not fail on regression.

checks.title: Critical-path end-to-end coverage
checks.expectation: At least one Playwright or Cypress spec covers the primary user journey for a user-facing application.
checks.violationSignal: No end-to-end specs exist in a user-facing application.

checks.title: No flaky-pattern signals
checks.expectation: Tests avoid fixed waits, ordering dependencies, and shared mutable state across tests.
checks.violationSignal: Fixed setTimeout or setInterval waits, ordering-dependent patterns, or shared mutable state are detected.

checks.title: Mocking at module boundaries
checks.expectation: Mocks are placed at module or network boundaries, not inside internal implementations of the system under test.
checks.violationSignal: Internal helpers used by the component under test are mocked, coupling tests to implementation details.

checks.title: Components have at least minimal coverage
checks.expectation: Every user-facing component identified by Graphify or folder heuristics has at least one related test file.
checks.violationSignal: User-facing components have no associated test file.
